observations_used: All four round-1 tail-refinement proposals were globally dominated.
(12,4), (13,3), (14,2), and (16,) remain the observed global area/WNS frontier.
(13,2,1) was dominated even by (14,2), despite having similar timing.
Introducing one-bit blocks near the tail did not improve the frontier.
Round 2 therefore preserves terminal blocks of width 3 or 4 and instead subdivides the large prefix.
hypothesis: A moderate subdivision of the large prefix may improve mapping or physical locality while retaining the favorable 3-4 bit terminal carry-select block.

proposals.rationale: Preserve a 4-bit tail while splitting the original 12-bit prefix into 9+3.
A more asymmetric prefix subdivision while preserving the strong 4-bit tail.
Preserve a 3-bit tail and divide the original 13-bit prefix into moderate blocks.
A sparse two-boundary architecture close to the strong (13,3) design without introducing one-bit blocks.
